strengths: Well-motivated research question about how LLMs learn algorithmic abstractions from code alone without I/O examples
Comprehensive experimental design spanning three datasets (random arithmetic, Leetcode, ciphers), multiple model scales (1B-8B), and thorough ablations
Non-obvious finding that code is dramatically more effective than semantically equivalent natural language (~10x better), which warrants investigation
Demonstrates interesting cross-domain transfer capabilities (Leetcode→Ciphers) suggesting algorithmic abstraction generalization
Clear presentation with effective figures and well-documented experimental methodology and hyperparameters
Shows practical insight that program training can improve robustness across input variations, partially addressing 'embers of autoregression'
weaknesses: Critically limited absolute performance (10-30% direct inference accuracy on random arithmetic) undermines claims about robust algorithmic learning; most strong results require chain-of-thought
Single seed experiments throughout with confidence intervals over generations only—no run-to-run variance reported, making it difficult to assess signal reliability
Insufficient mechanistic understanding: paper provides behavioral evidence of generalization but minimal insight into how models execute code or what representations enable it
Significant finetuning-pretraining gap: experiments conducted entirely in controlled finetuning regime while central claims about code benefits during pretraining remain speculative
Limited scope: experiments focus on relatively simple arithmetic and algorithms; unclear if mechanisms scale to complex real-world programs
Code vs. natural language finding inadequately investigated—why is code superior? Is it syntax, density, or compositionality? Only tested on one model (Llama-3.1-8B)
Composition results limited to chain-of-thought in smaller models; only GPT-4o shows implicit composition with uncertainty about additional inference compute
Data augmentation described as 'crucial' suggests brittleness; post-rationalized chain-of-thought ground truth accuracy uncertain; methodological fairness concerns in some comparisons
Robustness analysis limited to same-distribution held-out inputs; no adversarial or out-of-distribution testing
Incomplete analysis of key phenomena: limited investigation into what program properties affect learnability despite showing program length effects

strengths: Novel research question addressing an underexplored aspect of code training—whether LLMs can learn to evaluate programs from source code alone without I/O examples
Solid experimental methodology with clear two-stage finetuning designs, proper train/test splits, and comprehensive ablations across multiple datasets (Random Arithmetic, Leetcode, Ciphers)
Thorough evaluation across model scales (1B, 3B, 8B), inference modes (direct and chain-of-thought), and design choices (data augmentation, dataset size, I/O pair quantity)

Interesting empirical findings: code substantially outperforms natural language descriptions; RL enables retroactive generalization better than SFT; cross-domain transfer observed; more uniform robustness compared to I/O training
Good reproducibility: open-sourced datasets, detailed hyperparameters, reasonable computational requirements, clear problem formulation
Strong positioning within relevant literature (OOCR, algorithm distillation, algorithmic reasoning emergence) and clear, well-structured presentation
Practical implications for addressing 'embers of autoregression' problem and potential applications to model alignment through constitutional principles
weaknesses: Single seed limitation is critical: explicitly states 'due to computational constraints, all training is done for a single seed,' eliminating error estimates and making it impossible to assess robustness or variance of findings
Limited absolute performance raises questions about significance: Random Arithmetic ~28-30% for 8B model; Leetcode ~50-80%; unclear why these results matter practically
Synthetic/controlled datasets limit generalization claims: Random Arithmetic is artificially constructed; Leetcode results confounded by likely pretraining overlap; custom Ciphers unrealistic

Finetuning-only setup with large gap to pretraining regime: experiments use controlled finetuning, not pretraining; inductive biases differ significantly; claims about pretraining mechanisms are speculative
Mechanism remains opaque: paper demonstrates what happens but not how/why models store programs in weights or execute implicitly; no mechanistic interpretability, representation probing, or analysis

Implicit program execution has limited scope: performance on direct evaluation drops sharply for program length >3-4; composite programs fail for smaller models; chain-of-thought required for reliability
Critical dependence on data augmentation: Figure 2 shows performance collapses without augmentation; raises concern that PBB may be artifact of augmentation scheme rather than fundamental capability
Incomplete baseline comparisons: limited exploration of alternative curriculum strategies; augmentation ablation only partial; single-stage comparison relegated to appendix
Missing error analysis and failure mode investigation: no breakdown of error types, analysis of which programs cause failures, or discussion of limitation patterns
Overstated compositionality claims: low accuracy on composite programs for Llama; only GPT-4o shows meaningful implicit composition; footnote notes GPT-4o may use additional inference compute

strengths: Novel perspective on how LLMs can internalize procedural knowledge from declarative instructions through structured training curricula
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model families (Qwen3, Llama-3, GPT-4o), datasets (synthetic, Leetcode, custom ciphers, CFGs), and model scales with thorough ablations
Clear demonstration of sample efficiency: single instruction achieves comparable performance to ~100 execution examples in specific settings
Important safety implications: instructions in training data could elicit unintended behaviors at inference time
Well-designed two-stage curricula (proactive and retroactive) that both work, with stage-wise ablations clearly showing necessity of full pipeline
Good connection to partial evaluation framework provides useful intuition
Strong reproducibility: code release promised, clear training details, compute requirements disclosed
weaknesses: Critical reliability gap: PBB-trained execution significantly less reliable than in-context prompting, undermining the practical value proposition and making the 'worth 100 examples' claim potentially misleading
Unclear when practitioners would use PBB over simpler in-context prompting alternative—value proposition not convincingly established

Method novelty is moderate: proactive PBB closely mirrors existing implicit meta-learning work (Krasheninnikov et al. 2024), with limited algorithmic innovation beyond applying the curriculum to instruction internalization

Natural language instructions severely underperform compared to code (Figure 3, lower middle), but this critical limitation is relegated to appendix with speculative solutions rather than addressed head-on
Limited domain scope: predominantly synthetic data (random arithmetic, procedurally generated grammars) with unclear practical relevance; no NLP tasks or realistic procedural domains beyond Leetcode
Weak compositionality: models demonstrate limited ability to compose independently trained instructions, with direct inference failing for small models—fundamental limitation for practical utility

Limited theoretical understanding: 'latent learning' explanation lacks mechanistic depth; no investigation of what is actually learned in model parameters or whether the model truly 'compiles' vs. learns surface correlations
Context augmentation found essential to PBB but not deeply analyzed—design choice appears brittle with sensitivity to hyperparameters not characterized
Insufficient failure mode analysis: dramatic performance degradation with program length shown but not explained; no investigation of error types (partial execution, wrong outputs, etc.)

Comparison to simpler baseline (Appendix C, Figure 12) shows single-stage SFT approaches PBB performance with sufficient code repetition—unclear if sample efficiency advantage justifies added complexity

strengths: Novel curriculum-based approach to learning procedural knowledge from declarative instructions; elegant connection to partial evaluation
Comprehensive experimental design across multiple domains (algorithms, grammars), model families (Qwen, Llama, GPT-4o), and model sizes with well-motivated ablations
Rigorously demonstrates core claim: single instruction can substitute for ~100 execution examples in controlled settings
Both proactive and retroactive curricula validated; explicit ablations show both stages are necessary for strong performance
Insightful analysis of reliability, bias correction, representation formats (code vs. NL), and limited compositional capability
Important safety implications for data curation and model behavior; clear commitment to reproducibility with promised open-sourced code and datasets
Clear problem formulation with well-defined losses and formal framework
weaknesses: Limited domain scope: primarily synthetic datasets (Random Arithmetic with basic operations, procedurally generated CFGs); real-world validation on LeetCode shows retroactive PBB performs comparably to baseline, undermining practical value

Modest absolute performance on unpaired instructions (~37% for Random Arithmetic); substantial gap between paired/unpaired performance raises questions about practical applicability versus in-context instruction following
Natural language instructions perform substantially worse than code; dismissal as 'scaling issue' is unconvincing; severely limits real-world applicability

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: paper invokes 'latent learning' without deeply explaining why train execution gradients activate test knowledge; limited probing of representations learned in each stage

Context augmentation shown to be 'important' (20 templates per dataset); sensitivity to augmentation quality/quantity underexplored; Appendix C suggests single-stage SFT approaches PBB performance with repetitions, indicating augmentation + repetition does substantial work

Baseline comparisons limited to Algorithm Distillation; no comparison to few-shot in-context learning or other curriculum/meta-learning approaches; proactive PBB's Stage 1 meta-training cost not fully accounted in sample efficiency claims
Limited compositional capability: only shown for two-function composition; performance degrades substantially without explicit chain-of-thought reasoning
Modest statistical rigor: some experiments have overlapping confidence intervals yet differences are claimed; unclear replication counts for some results; no formal significance testing
